newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Krupp says EMU will have stable prices.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Krupp says EMU will have stable prices.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp said on Thursday that Europe's planned monetary union will enjoy a high degree of price stability.

He also said the Maastricht Treaty had created the institutional preconditions for the single currency, or euro, to be as stable as the mark, according to a summary of a speech he is due to make at a conference in Augsburg.
"There will be a high degree of price stability in the currency union," the summary said.
It added: "The European Central Bank is independent, it is primarily committed to price stability. Any form of state financing through the European central bank is ruled out."

Krupp said the European Central Bank (ECB) would be aided in its task of fighting inflation by the fact that wage bargainers in the monetary union would have to pay far closer attention to the impact of wage rises on inflation and employment than they do now.

In addition, the Maastricht Treaty contained sufficient provisions to monitor budgets and to prevent excessive deficits, so that dangers to monetary stability from high government borrowing could be ruled out.
